title: Puberty and Sexuality
summary: Physical and emotional changes during puberty, personal hygiene, values and decision-making about sexuality, consent, and the risks of teenage pregnancy, HIV and other STIs.

notes.text: **Puberty** is the stage of development, usually between about 9 and 16 years, when your body changes from a child's to an adult's and becomes able to reproduce. Everyone develops at their own pace: starting earlier or later than friends is normal.

rows: Testes and penis grow; wet dreams may occur
Oily skin and pimples; more sweat

items: Friends become more important; **peer pressure** may increase.
Worries about appearance and fitting in.
Shower or wash daily, especially after sport; use deodorant.
Wash your face to help prevent pimples; do not squeeze them.
During menstruation, change pads or tampons regularly (every 4 to 6 hours) and dispose of them properly.
Brush your teeth twice a day.

notes.text: **Sexuality** includes your body, feelings, relationships, gender identity and values, not just sexual activity. Your **values** (what is important to you) guide your decisions. Many teenagers choose **abstinence** (not having sex), which is the only 100% effective way to avoid pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

Freely and clearly agreeing to something. Consent must be given without pressure, can be withdrawn at any time, and cannot be given by someone who is drunk, drugged or asleep. In South Africa, the law sets the age of consent for sexual activity at 16.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: No one has the right to touch you in a way that makes you uncomfortable. If anyone abuses you, it is **never your fault**. Tell a trusted adult, or call Childline on **116**.

rows: Health risks for mother and baby; leaving school; financial and emotional stress
A virus that attacks the immune system; there is no cure, but antiretroviral treatment (ARVs) lets people live long, healthy lives
Other STIs (e.g. syphilis, gonorrhoea, herpes, chlamydia)
May cause pain, infertility and other health problems; many have no early symptoms

notes.text: **HIV is NOT spread** by hugging, sharing cups, toilets, swimming pools or mosquito bites. It is spread through unprotected sex, sharing needles, infected blood, and from mother to baby (which treatment can prevent). Youth-friendly clinics offer free, confidential advice, testing and contraception.

questions.prompt: Give THREE personal hygiene habits that are important during puberty.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): daily shower; deodorant; wash face; clean underwear daily; change sanitary products regularly; brush teeth

questions.prompt: Discuss THREE consequences of teenage pregnancy.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): health risks; dropping out of school; financial pressure; emotional stress; limited career opportunities; stigma

questions.prompt: Name TWO ways in which HIV is spread.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): unprotected sex; sharing needles; infected blood; mother to baby during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding
